## Prime-Agent System Prompt (ACP Template)

For file editing operations, the prime-agent runtime exposes a pre-installed `mcp` Python object with `list_tools` and `call_tool` methods. Use them to discover and invoke tools.

Example discovery and call:

```python
tools_list = await mcp.list_tools("tools")
for t in tools_list:
    print(t["name"], t["inputSchema"])

result = await mcp.call_tool("tools", "ox-bridge-write", {"path": "/tmp/x.py", "content": "# code here"})
print(result)
```

The `tools` MCP server exposes:
- `ox-bridge-write`: write a file (args: `path`, `content`)
- `ox-bridge-edit`: edit a file with hunks (args: `path`, `edits` = [{old, new}])
- `ox-bridge-read`: read a file region (args: `path`, `start`, `end`)

All bridging calls return synchronously. Print results to confirm before proceeding.

Serve a Three.js terrain demo page and verify it headlessly with Playwright. npm ESM project with three, vitest and playwright (its bundled chromium is already available; there is no display and no GPU, so never assert rendered pixels). src/terrain.js builds a seeded ridged terrain mesh (pure scene graph, unit-tested in test/terrain.test.js for determinism and height bounds with vitest). public/index.html plus src/main.js create the scene and attempt a WebGLRenderer inside try/catch; on failure the page must still set document.title to "terrain-ok" and write a div#status with the mesh's vertex count. scripts/screenshot.mjs starts a static server on 127.0.0.1 with node:http, launches chromium headless, collects console errors and pageerror events, waits for #status, screenshots to out/terrain.png, and exits nonzero on any console error. Assert the screenshot file is non-empty in test/page.test.js by invoking the script with node:child_process. npm test runs vitest run; everything green before you finish.

## Project layout

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | ESM (`"type": "module"`), deps: `three`, `vitest`, `playwright@1.62.1` (matches the preinstalled browser build) |
| `src/terrain.js` | Pure scene graph: mulberry32 PRNG → integer-hash value noise → 5-octave ridged multifractal (`(1-|2n-1|)²`) scaled into `[0, HEIGHT_MAX=10]`. Exports `createTerrain()`, `heightAt()`, `HEIGHT_MAX` |
| `test/terrain.test.js` | Bit-exact determinism across builds, seed divergence, height bounds over multiple seeds and 500 random `heightAt` probes, geometry well-formedness |
| `public/index.html` | Import map resolving bare `"three"` to `/node_modules/three/build/three.module.js` — no bundler needed |
| `src/main.js` | Builds terrain *first* (pure work, can't fail on GPU-less hosts), then attempts `WebGLRenderer` in try/catch; unconditionally sets `document.title = "terrain-ok"` and appends `div#status` with the vertex count |
| `scripts/screenshot.mjs` | `node:http` static server on `127.0.0.1:0` (ephemeral port, path-traversal guarded), launches headless chromium (`--no-sandbox --disable-gpu --use-gl=swiftshader`), collects console errors + `pageerror`s, waits for `#status`, screenshots to `out/terrain.png`, exits nonzero on any error or wrong title |
| `test/page.test.js` | Runs the script via `spawnSync`, asserts exit code 0, empty stderr, and a non-empty `out/terrain.png` |

Per the no-GPU constraint, no test asserts rendered pixels — only that the script exits cleanly and the PNG exists non-empty; WebGL rendering itself is best-effort inside the try/catch.
